title: Profile fields validate but are silently dropped by the mass-assignment guard
business_context: HabitTrack's users set their profile through PATCH /profile: display name, timezone (used to schedule reminders), and a marketing_opt_in consent flag (stored for GDPR compliance). Reminders are delivered per user timezone, so a wrong timezone means reminders at 3am. The endpoint returns the updated profile JSON and a 200 — the API contract is: what the client sends and what the server returns is what was stored.
user_request: Users report their reminder timezone keeps reverting to UTC and the marketing consent toggle doesn't stick, even though the app shows a green 'Profile saved' toast and the API returns 200. The name field saves fine. Find the actual root cause — don't just paper over the symptom — and fix persistence so every validated profile field is really stored. Also double-check your fix doesn't open the door to a client setting fields it must never set (like is_admin).

intentional_defect.summary: The form request validates timezone and marketing_opt_in, but User::$fillable lacks them — update($request->validated()) silently drops both, returning 200 with stale data.
intentional_defect.root_cause: Mass assignment guard: validated data contains timezone/marketing_opt_in, Eloquent's update() discards any attribute not in $fillable, and the controller returns the model — so the API reports success while nothing was persisted.
intentional_defect.why_it_looks_correct: Validation, controller, and API response all look correct in isolation, the visible tests (name) pass, and there is no error, log entry, or failed assertion pointing at the guard.

non_obvious_invariant: Every field that passes validation must actually persist; and no field outside the validated rule set (especially is_admin) may become mass-assignable through the fix.
expected_diagnosis: The agent must trace validated() → update() → $fillable and realize the guard silently filters attributes, then add exactly the legitimate fields (timezone, marketing_opt_in) to $fillable without loosening the guard beyond that.
safe_fix_constraints: PATCH /profile keeps its route, rules, and JSON contract.
The fix must not make is_admin (or any other privileged column) mass-assignable.
Fix the persistence mechanism, not just the symptom (e.g. no silent second save() call that bypasses the API contract).
failure_explanation: Users' reminders fire at 3am local time (timezone never stored), consent flags never change (a GDPR compliance incident in waiting), and the 200-with-stale-data response masks the bug from both clients and support. An agent 'fixing' it by switching to $request->all() would let any authenticated user PATCH is_admin=true and escalate to administrator — a privilege-escalation hole.
